Owner: Operator-approved pinned tool/input tree capture. Removal: Remove only when PinnedTree capture owns an equivalent resolved-root mechanism; no inference that content pinning or native input I/O disappears. Owner: Operator-owned platform input capture. Resolve the selected platform source root before collecting the exact platform build inputs. Removal: Retire only if platform input capture no longer resolves this source root; preserve actual file digest admission separately. Limits: Immediate root must be a real directory, then checked pinning/collection. Canonicalization is a pathname observation, not provider authority, an inode lock or a race-resistant containment guarantee.

Owner: Operator-owned toolchain input capture. Resolve the separate selected toolchain root before platform capture pins the required compiler/toolchain files. Removal: Retire only when selected toolchain path resolution is replaced by an equivalent owned input capture; toolchain content pins remain required. Limits: Immediate toolchain root must be a real directory, with later file content pins. No inode continuity or hostile ancestor/rename guarantee is established by canonicalization.

Owner: Operator-approved trusted build runner capture. Resolve the runner executable pathname after pin_file verifies its bytes and executable permission for the builder binding. Removal: Retire only if the trusted runner capture ceases to retain this resolved executable path; keep actual executable/digest and builder-binding checks. Limits: Explicit operator capability with digest/executable checks, Rust/offline-registry capture and fixed recipe binding. Path resolution does not itself validate the executable digest at subsequent launch or prove safe host state.

Owner: Operator-owned fixed build evidence storage. Resolve the private output root before execution-specific locking, isolated job/result directories and evidence publication. Removal: Remove only if fixed local build evidence storage no longer uses this path resolution; preserve private outputs, execution identity and existing-evidence checks. Limits: private_directory establishes the immediate real directory and0700 on Unix; execution digest selects local names. No quota, ownership-of-ancestor or TOCTOU guarantee follows from canonicalization.

Owner: Operator-owned local build directory setup. Check whether the private build/input directory already exists before creating it and applying the existing real-directory/Unix0700 checks. Removal: Retire only if this exact directory setup no longer distinguishes existing and new local state; retain actual directory/type/permission checks. Limits: exists is a state probe that can collapse I/O errors; create_dir_all and symlink_metadata supply later operation errors/type refusal. No atomic freshness or authority proof is claimed.
